## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

According to the narrative framework preserved in V. Fausböll's edition, the Buddha delivered this discourse while residing at Jetavana about a greengrocer lay-disciple (*paṇṇikaupāsaka*) [Fausböll 1879]. The layman, having tested the virtue of his daughter—who was known for her perpetually smiling demeanor—before giving her in marriage to a youth of good family, recounted the incident to the Buddha [Fausböll 1879].

The central verse opens with the line *Sabbo loko attamano ahosi* ("All the world is on pleasure bent"), observing that while the rest of the world takes pleasure in sensual indulgence, the innocent daughter Seggu is unacquainted with worldly or sexual ways (*gāmadhamma*) and weeps when taken by the hand in the woods [Fausböll 1879]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the greengrocer attains the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*), and the Buddha reveals the previous rebirths: the father and daughter were identical in both lifetimes, while the Bodhisatta was the tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*) who bore witness to the father testing his daughter [Fausböll 1879].
